map.string: How the numeric keypad controls your avatar. 0 = behaves like the normal arrow keys; 1 = numpad moves the avatar when NumLock is off (types digits when on); 2 = numpad always moves the avatar regardless of NumLock (use if you have no NumLock key).

FAudio output device id (WASAPI device string on Windows, SDL device id elsewhere). Empty string uses the system default. Per-backend key so a saved id from one backend doesn't get mis-applied if the user switches engines.

OpenAL output device name (which also serves as its id — OpenAL doesn't surface a separate GUID). Empty string uses the system default. Per-backend key so a saved id from one backend doesn't get mis-applied if the user switches engines.

FMOD output device id (FMOD_GUID in canonical "{XXXXXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX}" form). Empty string uses driver 0 / system default. Per-backend key so a saved id from one backend doesn't get mis-applied if the user switches engines.

FAudio backend: F3DAudio emitter InnerRadius in metres. Below this distance source channels diffuse to all speakers; above, clean directional pan. Applies live; new value is picked up on the next 3D update tick.

I3DL2 reverb preset applied by whichever audio backend supports reverb (FAudio always, OpenAL when ALC_EXT_EFX is present, FMOD always). PLAIN is the open-outdoor default; case-insensitive. Recognised: DEFAULT, GENERIC, PADDEDCELL, ROOM, BATHROOM, LIVINGROOM, STONEROOM, AUDITORIUM, CONCERTHALL, CAVE, ARENA, HANGAR, CARPETEDHALLWAY, HALLWAY, STONECORRIDOR, ALLEY, FOREST, CITY, MOUNTAINS, QUARRY, PLAIN, PARKINGLOT, SEWERPIPE, UNDERWATER, SMALLROOM. DEFAULT / SMALLROOM are mapped to backend-specific equivalents where the underlying preset table doesn't carry them by name. Applies live; preset changes are pushed to the engine on the next signal callback.

FAudio backend: reverb wet-send level. Scales F3DAudio's dsp.ReverbLevel per source before writing the per-source -> reverb-submix matrix. 0 disables reverb. The default (0.05) is intentionally subtle because the FAudioFX reverb tail is fairly pronounced at full strength. Applies live; picked up on the next update tick.

FAudio backend: enable the FAPOFX FXMasteringLimiter on the mastering voice. Prevents the device-side integer quantizer from clipping when many sources sum past unity in the float-internal mix (typical SL scenes with dozens of simultaneous sources). Disable only if you specifically want raw post-mix peaks, accepting the resulting distortion. Applies live; toggles the FAPO's enabled state without rebuilding the chain.

FAudio backend: gain-recovery time of the master limiter in milliseconds. FAPOFX range is [1, 20]; default 6. Lower = snappier release (more transparent on percussive material but can pump on sustained peaks); higher = smoother recovery at the cost of slightly attenuated transients after a hit. Applies live.

FAudio backend: master limiter loudness/threshold parameter. FAPOFX range is [1, 1800]; default 1000. Higher values leave more headroom before the limiter engages (less aggressive); lower values compress earlier (more aggressive). MSDN doesn't document the unit; treat as a subjective dial. Applies live.

OpenAL backend (EFX): reverb wet-send level, written directly to AL_EFFECTSLOT_GAIN on the auxiliary effect slot. 0 disables; range [0, 1]. The default (0.25) is higher than the FAudio key because the EFX slot-gain is a single global multiplier on the whole effect output rather than a per-source coefficient, so it needs less scaling to feel similarly "subtle". Applies live.

FMOD backend: reverb wet-send level, applied per channel via Channel::setReverbProperties on instance 0. Range [0, 1]; 0 disables. The default (0.15) sits between FAudio's per-source coefficient and OpenAL's slot-gain because FMOD's wet scalar interacts with the per-channel mix differently from either. Applies live.

Depth of the slow random-walk gain modulator applied by LLWindGen to the procedural wind drone. 0 disables gustiness entirely and the synth runs bit-identically to the historical steady drone. 1 means ±100% gain modulation, picked from a fresh random target every ~1.5 seconds and interpolated smoothly. Applies live across all reverb-capable backends; takes effect on the next synthesised wind sample.

Strength of the altitude-dependent gain lift applied to the wind drone when the camera is above water. 0 disables the boost entirely; 1 scales wind gain by up to 1.5x at the 4096m sim ceiling, following a square-root curve so the transition off the ground is perceptible without becoming overwhelming at typical skybox altitudes. The underwater muffle (cutoff drop + gain attenuation when the camera is submerged) is always on and not gated by this setting. Applies live; takes effect on the next coefficient update tick.

Which avatar passes cast shadows. 0 = opaque only, 1 = opaque + alpha mask, 2 = full (also alpha blend). Lower values speed up crowd scenes by skipping the expensive alpha-blend avatar shadow pass across all cascades.

How sun shadow cascades are culled. 0 = cull and sort each cascade separately (default). 1 = cull and sort once against a frustum spanning all cascades, sharing the result (less CPU per frame, more GPU vertex work per cascade). Experimental.
Replace legacy glow with HDR bloom pyramid (pre-tonemap). 0 = legacy glow, 1 = HDR bloom.
HDR bloom luminance threshold in linear light. Values above this bloom; below, fall off softly via the knee. 1.0 = roughly "brighter than white".
Soft-knee width below the bloom threshold. Wider values give a softer, more gradual bloom onset. Range 0 to 1.
Number of bloom pyramid mip levels. More mips = wider, softer bloom. Clamped to [3, 7].

Base bloom pyramid resolution relative to scene. 0 = full, 1 = 3/4, 2 = half, 3 = quarter, 4 = eighth. Higher = faster and wider bloom reach per mip, with bilinear upscale at composite. Clamped to [0, 4].
Bloom upsample tent-filter radius multiplier. 1.0 = adjacent-texel taps. Values >1 widen the bloom per octave; >~2.5 starts to alias because the tent skips source texels.
Multiplier applied to alpha-tagged glow (legacy prim glow parameter) when fed into HDR bloom. Compensates for pre-tonemap composite so prim-glow halos match legacy brightness.

HDR bloom composite strength. Multiplies the final bloom pyramid before it is additively blended into the scene. Independent of RenderGlowStrength so HDR bloom and legacy glow can be tuned separately.

Enable the halation signal in HDR bloom. When off, the bloom pyramid allocates as R11F_G11F_B10F (half the bandwidth of RGBA16F) and skips the warmth extract and tinted composite. Requires RenderBloomHDR.
Photographic halation (warm halo around bright highlights). 0 disables. 0.25 is a gentle cinematic feel. Requires RenderBloomHalation.
Tint color for the halation halo (linear RGB). Default is a warm amber. Requires RenderBloomHalation.
Overall intensity of the chromatic aberration fringe. 0 disables the effect. 0.15 gives a subtle cinema lens feel; 0.5 is heavy. Range 0 to 1.
How quickly the aberration grows from the screen center outward. 1 is a linear ramp; higher values keep the center clean and push fringing to the edges. Range 0.5 to 4.
Rotates the red/blue split direction, in degrees. 0 is horizontal; 90 is vertical. Only meaningful when Anisotropy is nonzero. Range 0 to 360.
Stretches the fringe along the angle axis. 0 gives an even radial fringe; positive values elongate it into a directional smear for anamorphic-style aberration. Range -1 to 1.
Red channel horizontal offset direction. -1 shifts red inward on the X axis, +1 outward. Combined with RY for per-channel fringe direction. Range -1 to 1.
Red channel vertical offset direction. Pairs with OffsetRX. 0 keeps red split purely horizontal. Range -1 to 1.
Blue channel horizontal offset direction. Typically opposite sign of OffsetRX for a standard red/blue split. Range -1 to 1.
Blue channel vertical offset direction. Pairs with OffsetBX. 0 keeps blue split purely horizontal. Range -1 to 1.
Name of image file for color grading LUT(TGA, PNG, or WebP)
Strength of the color grading LUT effect
Split toning strength for shadows and highlights. 0 disables the effect; 0.5 is a natural cinematic push. Tints shadows and highlights without shifting overall brightness.
Slides the midpoint between shadow and highlight tints. Negative values widen shadows (good for dark scenes); positive values widen highlights (good for bright scenes). Range -1 to 1.
Target color for shadow tones. Neutral gray (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) is identity. Try cool teal (0.35, 0.5, 0.55) for classic teal-and-orange looks.
Target color for highlight tones. Neutral gray (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) is identity. Try warm amber (0.6, 0.5, 0.4) to complement teal shadows.
Target color for midtones. Neutral gray (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) is identity. Warm tints like (0.55, 0.5, 0.45) flatter skin tones.
Midtone tint strength, independent from shadow/highlight amount. 0 disables; subtle values (0.15-0.35) add mood without muddying skin.

White balance temperature shift, in Kelvin relative to neutral daylight. Negative warms the image, positive cools it. Range -5000 to +5000. Default 0. Try -2500 tungsten glow, -1000 golden hour, +1500 blue hour, +3000 moonlit.

Green/magenta tint, perpendicular to the temperature axis. Negative pushes magenta, positive pushes green. Range -1 to +1. Default 0. Try -0.4 cyberpunk magenta, +0.4 fluorescent green, +0.75 Matrix green.

Shadow lift (R,G,B): adds to the darkest tones to raise the black floor and tint shadows. Per-channel range -0.5 to +0.5. Default (0,0,0). Try (0.02,0.02,0.05) cool shadow mist, (0.05,0.03,0) warm lift, negatives crush toward black.

Midtone gamma (R,G,B): bends the middle of the tonal range without moving blacks or whites. Below 1 brightens mids, above 1 darkens them. Per-channel range 0.5 to 1.5. Default (1,1,1). Try (0.9,0.9,0.9) open mids, (1.1,1.0,0.95) warm mids.

Highlight gain (R,G,B): multiplies the brightest tones to boost, clip, or tint whites. Per-channel range 0.5 to 1.5. Default (1,1,1). Try (1.05,1.02,0.95) warm highlights, (0.95,1.0,1.05) cool highlights, uniform <1 to tame blowouts.
Crushes values at or below this level to pure black. 0 is identity, 0.05 deepens blacks cinematically, 0.1+ starts clipping shadow detail.
Clips values at or above this level to pure white. 1 is identity, 0.95 blooms highlights, 0.9 produces a washed bleach-bypass look.
Shifts the whole image lighter or darker. Range -0.5 to 0.5; small values (±0.05) are already noticeable.
S-curve around midgray. 1 is identity; less than 1 flattens (matte film look), greater than 1 punches (values above 1.3 start clipping).
Recovers (negative) or boosts (positive) highlights without touching midtones. Use -0.3 to pull blown skies back from clipping.
Lifts (positive) or crushes (negative) shadows without touching midtones. Use +0.2 to reveal shadow detail in dark scenes.
Uniform saturation. 1 is identity, 0 is black-and-white, 1.2 is punchy, 1.5 is heavily stylized.
Smart saturation that pushes muted colors harder than already-saturated ones. Skin-friendly; range -1 to 1, 0.3 is a subtle lift.
Rotates all hues around the color wheel in degrees. Range -180 to 180. 30 warms everything; 180 is a full complement (inverted).
Per-channel filmic curve toe point (RGB). Pixels at or below this input level flatten toward black. Try (0.05, 0.05, 0.1) to lift shadow blues.
Per-channel filmic curve shoulder point (RGB). Pixels at or above this input level flatten toward white. Lower values (around 0.85) give a tighter roll-off.
Per-channel curve blend strength (RGB). 0 disables; 0.4 is typical film, differing values per channel create cross-process looks.
Color vision deficiency effect mode - 0 = off, 1 = protanopia (no L cones), 2 = deuteranopia (no M cones), 3 = tritanopia (no S cones)
[0, 1] Strength of applied color vision deficiency effect

color of the film grain. vec3(1) = neutral gray. Try vec3(1.0, 0.9, 0.8) for warm film grain, vec3(0.8, 0.9, 1.0) for cool video noise

Master intensity of the lens flare effect. 0 turns it off entirely; 1 is full strength. Use this as the on/off switch.
How far the horizontal anamorphic streak stretches across the screen. 0.5 reaches halfway; 1.0 crosses the full width. Range 0.01 to 2.
How quickly the streak fades toward its tips. Lower values leave a longer visible tail; higher values make the streak fade in close to the sun. Range 0.1 to 10.
Vertical thickness of the streak as a fraction of the screen. Lower is a thin hairline, higher is a soft horizontal band. Range 0 to 1.
Brightness multiplier for just the streak, separate from the master strength. 1 is neutral; higher boosts the streak without affecting the glow/ghosts. Range 0 to 5.
Color of the horizontal streak. The default cool blue mimics coated anamorphic cinema lenses; try warm tones for sci-fi or golden hour looks.
Red/blue color separation along the streak for a chromatic fringe look. 0 is clean; 1 gives a strong rainbow split. Range 0 to 1.
Size of the soft glow bloom directly around the sun. Small values hug the light; larger values create a wider halo of brightness. Range 0.01 to 0.5.
Softness of the central glow. Lower values give a gentle, spread-out bloom; higher values keep it tight and punchy. Range 1 to 30.
Intensity of the soft central glow around the sun. 0 disables the glow; 1 is neutral; higher boosts it. Range 0 to 5.
Number of lens ghost circles placed along the line from the sun through the screen center. Shape control only; use RenderLensFlareGhost to toggle the effect. Range 0 to 8.
Distance between consecutive ghosts. Smaller packs them near the sun; larger spreads them across the screen. Range 0.1 to 1.
Intensity of the lens ghost circles. 0 disables ghosts; 1 is neutral; higher boosts them. Range 0 to 5.
Radius of the halo ring that appears opposite the sun through screen center. Shape control only; use RenderLensFlareHalo to toggle the effect. Range 0.01 to 1.
Thickness of the halo ring. Smaller is a crisp hoop; larger is a soft diffuse ring. Range 0.01 to 0.5.
Intensity of the halo ring opposite the sun. 0 disables the halo; 1 is neutral; higher boosts it. Range 0 to 5.
Intensity of the starburst (diffraction-spike) pattern radiating from the sun, like aperture blades in a camera. 0 disables it. Range 0 to 5.
Number of aperture-like spikes in the starburst. Real cameras typically show 2x the blade count (6-blade = 12 spikes, etc). Range 1 to 32.
How crisp the starburst spikes look. Low values produce soft, wide rays; high values produce thin, needle-like beams. Range 1 to 256.
Length of the starburst spikes. 0 is short and tight to the sun; 1 lets them reach far across the screen. Range 0 to 1.
How wide the sun-occlusion test samples the scene depth. Larger values let thin geometry (foliage, wires) dim the flare more gracefully. Range 0.005 to 0.1.
Number of depth samples for sun-occlusion testing. Higher values give smoother partial occlusion transitions at a small performance cost. Range 1 to 32.
